target_customer: Startups and developers who need to send SMS and RCS messages
problem: SMS APIs such as Twilio are costly and 10DLC campaign approval takes weeks; Sendo offered a cheaper, developer friendly API with faster compliance.
product_category: Developer tools, SMS and RCS API

founders.name: Nick Rubin
previous_startups: A viral Chrome extension, an Ethereum prediction market (listed as projects on YC page)

competitors.name: Twilio
competitors.what: Market leading SMS and voice API
competitors.traction_then: Named by Sendo as the main alternative, savings claim of 40 percent or more

technical_complexity.rationale: Wrapper over carrier aggregators with a dashboard and 10DLC registration workflow; compliance handling was the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: Resold carrier capacity with no data or network moat; many SMS API vendors competed on price.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents responding to Sendo specifically.

market_need_then: Developers complained about Twilio pricing and weeks long 10DLC approvals after US carriers tightened A2P rules; this is from Sendo's own pitch, not an independent source.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand; the name resembles Sendo the Vietnamese marketplace and other messaging tools.

outcome_analysis: The YC directory marks Sendo Inactive with a team of one, yet sendo.dev and a status page appear live in 2026 listings and no shutdown or acquisition was found, so the outcome is unclear. A single founder team in a commodity usage priced SMS market with large incumbents suggests thin differentiation, but no source states a cause.
notes: The 500K pre-seed rests on a single database (VCBacked, Crunchbase shows a pre-seed with no amount). sendo.dev fetch returned only a title. A mirror lists the company active while YC lists Inactive. Founders' prior employers are not listed on the YC page. Pinnacle is a separate YC RCS API company, not Sendo.
